prompt: Implement the State pattern: three state objects (draft, review, published) decide every transition themselves, while DocumentWorkflow only swaps the current state and counts the changes that really happened.
explanation: Each state class answers the same three questions in its own way, so the rules of the workflow live in the states rather than in a growing switch statement. A state that refuses a request returns this, which is how the workflow can tell a real transition from a no-op: compare the returned state with the current one before counting. Published returns itself for every request, which makes it a terminal state without any extra code.
hints: Only three transitions actually move anywhere: Draft.onSubmit -> Review, Review.onApprove -> Published, Review.onReject -> Draft. Everything else returns this.
state() is simply current.label() -- no comparisons needed.
Write one private helper that takes the next state, and only when next != current assigns it and increases the counters; reject() passes a flag so it can also count a rejection.
